newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN Amro may buy more banks in Eastern Europe.
newsitem.headline: ABN Amro may buy more banks in Eastern Europe.

text.p: Dutch banking group ABN Amro is considering buying more banks in Eastern and Central Europe but has nothing concrete to announce, chairman Jan Kalff said on Thursday.

"There's nothing in the pipeline which can be announced in the next couple of months but there are some realistic cases that we are studying at the moment, also in Central and Eastern Europe," Kalff told a news conference while on a visit to Magyar Hitel Bank, its Hungarian subsidiary.
ABN Amro recently made its biggest bank purchase ever, buying Standard Federal, the largest savings bank in the U.S. Midwest, for $1.9 billion.
"Last year we studied 50 acquisition possibilities," he added. "That's an enormous amount of work and we have done only five or so out of the 50, so you turn down many more than you do."

Zsigmond Jarai, chief executive of Magyar Hitel Bank, said the bank, in which ABN Amro purchased an 89.23 percent stake last year for $89.23 million, was integrating itself into the ABN Amro network and was developing financial products that could eventually be exported and used in other Eastern European countries.
Kalff added that he met earlier in the day with Gyorgy Suranyi, the president of the National Bank of Hungary, and said he was impressed with the progress made by the Hungarian economy.
"We had a lengthy discussion with the governor of the central bank and if I compare notes with one or two years ago then the change for the better is obvious," Kalff said.
"Not everything is going well but surely that is the case in Holland, too

"...On average the situation (in Hungary) is improving, inflation is coming down. The stabiility of the currency is becoming better, the balance of payments is gradually improving and the deficit of the government is gradually decreasing.
"We would be ready to lead manage a bond issue for Hungary and that would not have been another situation four or five years ago.
"The very fact that Hungary is not in a need for money is already a very good sign in itself."
